title: Pocket synopsis: longwalk notes
content:
Quick brain-dump after a longwalk listening to talks + skimming a batch of papers. This is messy — intended as a pocket notebook for ideas to test and refs to pull into more formal writeups.

Top-level takeaways
- Prefix/patching heuristics keep surfacing as low-effort wins: cheap KV-pruning + token-level frequency heuristics reduce memory without retraining. Good for Hosted/Dedicated where memory pressure is a real cost.
- Eviction strategies matter more than raw cache size for user-facing latency: LRU is ok, but TTL + relevance score (recency * similarity) yields better observed utility on chat-like traces.
- Quantized KV (4/8-bit) can be surprisingly stable if we bias-restore attention logits; still need checks for rare token amplification.
- Eval setups are brittle: synthetic long-context tasks exaggerate benefits. Use mixed-length real chat logs + engineered probes.

Papers / ideas skimmed (notes to self)
- Paper A (long-context transformer optimizations): interesting kernel fusion trick for cross-attention that reduces memcopy overhead on A100/MI250. Try porting small patch to runtime.
- Paper B (kv-compression): block-wise SVD-like compression per attention head; cheap to compute offline, incremental updates possible for hot prefixes. Run small-scale sim of accuracy vs cache-size on our convo dataset.
- Blog: practical batching/buffer sizing heuristics for interactive workloads — aligns with Redwood Optimize suggestions but missing guidance for multi-tenant Dedicated pools. Add a note to product.

Experiments to spin up (priority ordering)
1) Eviction ablation: implement recency*semantic_relevance score in local test harness. Metric: next-token perplexity on points that would have been evicted by LRU. (Target 2 days)
2) Quantized-KV sanity: convert stored KV to 4-bit with bias-restoration trick + run hallucination probes on long prompts. Watch for tail-token spikes. (Target 1 week)
3) Kernel patch prototype: bring kernel fusion patch into small microbench harness (1-GPU). Measure memcpy and kernel launch times for seqlen=8k. (Target 2 weeks)
4) Eval augmentation: construct mixed-length trace generator combining real user snippets (anonymized) + adversarial prefix mutations to better surface edge regressions. (Target ongoing)

Notes on evaluation design (lean, pragmatic)
- Always include a cost axis: tokens served per second and memory footprint observed. If quality delta small but cost delta large, flag as not production-ready.
- Canary composition: sample 10% of traffic with aggressive kv-prune; measure error surface + latency tail. If no regressions for 24h, expand.
- Lightweight probes: question-answer pairs that rely on earliest context (index-lookup style) are high-signal for eviction harms. Keep a small curated set.

Prompt engineering / user-facing heuristics
- Prompt prefix-metadata: insert short TTL markers for system-level instructions so we can preferentially preserve them. Low overhead and robust.
- Chunked reference pointers: for long docs, store compact summary tokens in KV cache (e.g., 64-token summary embeddings as synthetic tokens) — cheaper than keeping entire doc. Test distillation vs naive keep-all.

Operational concerns for Redwood deployments
- Hosted: aggressive caching is fine, but need transparent instrumentation surfaced in Console (per-route cache-hit rate, eviction counts). Add a small ticket to product ops.
- Dedicated: offer a knob for KV-compression policy per pool. Sales/engineers will want simple defaults + a cost-savings estimate.
- Private: offline compression and controlled kernel changes are easier — good candidate for early adopter customers.

Open questions / uncertainties
- How stable are quantized-KV methods across model families (decoder-only vs encoder-decoder)? Need to test with at least two open models.
- Is semantic_relevance computation cheap enough in high-throughput pathways? Might need approximate sim (LSH) — complexity tradeoff.
- Failure modes: compressed KV plus out-of-distribution prompts — risk of subtle context corruption. Design checks to detect sudden accuracy drops.

Action items (short):
- [ ] Spin up eviction ablation harness (assign: Aisha)
- [ ] Small PR prototype for 4-bit KV serialization (assign: Jonah)
- [ ] Draft short note for Console team: include cache telemetry (assign: Mira)
- [ ] Collect 200 anonymized multi-turn traces for mixed-length eval (low effort, high value)

Random fragments / heuristics worth saving here:
- heuristic: prefer preserving tokens that are short and contain repeated named entities + system roles — often high utility.
- shorthand: "longwalk" = overnight skims + walk-through experiments (good input for creative thinking)
- mental model: KV cache ~= short-term episodic memory; better eviction improves "working memory" not long-term knowledge.

References to bookmark:
- arXiv paper on kv compression (linked above)
- blog post on batching heuristics (Slack: #infra-discuss thread id 6789)
- internal PR: github.com/redwood-inference/kv-cache-experiments/pull/42

Notes-to-self end. Will refine into a short tech note for the team next week.
